section: Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme - Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Trishul, Nag
subsections: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service
Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the type and fuel of the Prithvi missile?
o: Anti-tank guided missile using liquid fuel
Surface-to-surface intercontinental ballistic missile using cryogenic fuel
Surface-to-surface short-range ballistic missile using liquid fuel
accepted.x: Prithvi is a surface-to-surface short-range ballistic missile with a range of 150–350 km and uses liquid fuel.
accepted.tq: Match the missile’s role with its characteristic propellant.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Prithvi missile:
1. Prithvi was the first missile developed under the IGMDP.
2. Prithvi-I is operated by the Army.
3. Prithvi-II is operated by the Air Force.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Prithvi was the first IGMDP missile; Prithvi-I serves the Army and Prithvi-II serves the Air Force.
accepted.tq: Use service allocation and the first-development distinction together.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following missiles is correctly matched with its operating service?
1. Prithvi-I — Army
2. Prithvi-II — Air Force
3. Agni — Strategic Forces Command
4. Nag — Army
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four matches are correct. The listed services are Army for Prithvi-I and Nag, Air Force for Prithvi-II, and Strategic Forces Command for Agni.
accepted.tq: Check each service association independently before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Prithvi-II is distinguished from Prithvi-I by which one of the following combinations?
o: 150 km range and 4–7 km payload capacity
5,000 km range and three-stage solid propulsion
700 km range and two-stage solid propulsion
accepted.x: Prithvi-II has a range of 350 km and a payload capacity of 500–1,000 kg. Prithvi-I has a range of 150 km.
accepted.tq: Compare the two closely related variants by range and payload.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Prithvi-II, consider the following statements:
1. It was first tested in 1996.
2. It was inducted in 2003.
3. It is a naval, ship-launched missile.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Prithvi-II was first tested in 1996 and inducted in 2003. The naval, ship-launched version is Dhanush, not Prithvi-II.
accepted.tq: Spot the swapped variant in a three-statement question.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Dhanush, in the context of the Prithvi family, refers to the:
o: Mobile version of Prithvi-I for the Army
Interceptor version of Prithvi for exo-atmospheric defence
accepted.x: Dhanush is the naval, ship-launched version of the Prithvi missile.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the naval derivative from the Army and Air Force variants.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations is correct regarding the three missile families?
1. Akash — medium-range surface-to-air missile
2. Trishul — short-range, low-level surface-to-air missile
3. Nag — third-generation anti-tank guided missile
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Akash is a medium-range SAM, Trishul is a short-range low-level SAM, and Nag is a third-generation ATGM.
accepted.tq: Separate missile classification by target and launch role.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Akash missile is correctly described by which one of the following?
o: A subsonic anti-tank missile with a range of 4–7 km
A medium-range SAM travelling at about Mach 2.5 and reaching 18 km altitude
A liquid-fuel surface-to-surface missile with a range of 150 km
A three-stage ballistic missile with a range exceeding 5,000 km
accepted.x: Akash is a medium-range surface-to-air missile with a range of about 25–30 km, a speed of approximately Mach 2.5 and an altitude capability of 18 km.
accepted.tq: Use speed and altitude to identify the correct missile profile.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Trishul is NOT correct?
o: Its commonly cited range is about 9 km.
It was inducted into regular service after successful development.
It is a short-range, low-level surface-to-air missile.
It uses solid fuel with thrust vector control.
accepted.x: Trishul was never inducted into regular service and the programme was closed in 2008. It is a short-range low-level SAM using solid fuel with thrust vector control.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong service-status statement rather than the missile’s technical features.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The IGMDP development phases were arranged in which one of the following chronological sequences?
o: Agni 1992–2008; Prithvi and Trishul 1984–89; Nag and Akash 1989–92
Prithvi and Trishul 1984–89; Nag and Akash 1989–92; Agni 1992–2008
Nag and Akash 1984–89; Agni 1989–92; Prithvi and Trishul 1992–2008
Prithvi and Trishul 1989–92; Nag and Akash 1992–2008; Agni 1984–89
accepted.x: The phases were Prithvi and Trishul during 1984–89, Nag and Akash during 1989–92, and Agni during 1992–2008.
accepted.tq: Arrange the programme phases by their starting years.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. Long-range tracking system — IGMDP spin-off
2. Ring laser gyros — IGMDP spin-off
3. Radomes — IGMDP spin-off
4. Composites — IGMDP spin-off
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Long-range tracking systems, composites, ring laser gyros and radomes are all listed as spin-offs of the missile development effort.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete set of related technological spin-offs.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
1. Nag — 4–7 km
2. Trishul — about 9 km
3. Akash — about 25–30 km
4. Agni — 4–7 km
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Agni is a ballistic missile family with ranges from about 700 km to more than 5,000 km, not 4–7 km. The other ranges are associated with Nag, Trishul and Akash respectively.
accepted.tq: Use range-class elimination to expose the misplaced missile.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Prithvi-I, Prithvi-II and Agni-I are nuclear-capable.
2. The Army fires these missiles from mobile transporter-erector-launcher trucks.
3. All three use liquid fuel.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The first two statements are correct. Agni-I uses solid fuel, whereas Prithvi-I and Prithvi-II use liquid fuel; therefore statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Separate the common operational feature from the differing propulsion feature.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the two Indian ballistic-missile defence interceptors?
o: PAD is exo-atmospheric at 50–80 km, whereas AAD is endo-atmospheric at 15–30 km.
PAD is endo-atmospheric, whereas AAD is exo-atmospheric.
Both PAD and AAD are anti-tank missiles operating below 10 km.
Both PAD and AAD are surface-to-surface missiles using liquid fuel.
accepted.x: Prithvi Air Defence or Pradyumna is an exo-atmospheric interceptor operating at 50–80 km altitude, while AAD or Ashwin is an endo-atmospheric interceptor operating at 15–30 km.
accepted.tq: Discriminate paired systems by atmospheric layer and altitude.
accepted.sec: IGMDP missiles - type, range class, service  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Agni-I is best described as a:
o: Two-stage liquid-fuel missile of about 2,000–3,000 km range
Single-stage solid-fuel missile of about 700–800 km range
Single-stage liquid-fuel missile of about 150 km range
Three-stage solid-fuel missile of about 5,000 km range
accepted.x: Agni-I is a single-stage solid-fuel missile with a range of about 700–800 km and is approximately 15 metres long.
accepted.tq: Identify the missile from its stage, fuel and range combination.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following correctly matches Agni-II and Agni-III with their range and stage configuration?
1. Agni-II — 2,000–3,000 km, two-stage solid
2. Agni-III — about 3,500 km, two-stage solid
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Agni-II has a range of 2,000–3,000 km and Agni-III has a range of about 3,500 km; both are two-stage solid-fuel missiles.
accepted.tq: Compare adjacent Agni variants using both range and stages.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Agni-III, consider the following statements:
1. Its standard range is about 3,500 km.
2. It is a two-stage solid-fuel missile.
3. Its payload is approximately 1,500–2,500 kg.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct for Agni-III. A 2026 current-affairs source also gave a wider 3,000–5,000 km figure, but the standard APPSC figure is about 3,500 km.
accepted.tq: Retain the standard examination figure while checking the complete technical profile.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with Agni-IV?
accepted.x: Agni-IV is a two-stage solid-fuel, road-mobile MRBM with a range of about 4,000 km. Three-stage solid propulsion belongs to Agni-V.
accepted.tq: Use the stage-count trap to distinguish Agni-IV from Agni-V.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Agni-IV incorporates which one of the following combinations of navigation and accuracy features?
o: RINS and MINGS navigation with CEP below 100 metres
Satellite navigation only with no specialised onboard navigation
Only optical navigation with CEP above 1,000 metres
Ring laser gyros without any inertial navigation system
accepted.x: Agni-IV uses RINS and MINGS navigation systems and has a circular error probable (CEP) of less than 100 metres.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise technical combination rather than a generic navigation claim.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Agni-V:
1. It is a three-stage solid-fuel missile.
2. It is canister-launched.
3. Its range is stated as 5,000 km or more.
4. MIRV technology has been tested with it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Agni-V is a three-stage solid-fuel, canister-launched missile with a stated range of 5,000 km or more, and MIRV capability has been tested with it.
accepted.tq: Combine propulsion, launch mode, range and payload-technology clues.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Regarding the classification of Agni-V, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
o: It is classified as an SRBM because it is canister-launched.
It is a proposed missile and has not been associated with MIRV testing.
Its stated 5,000 km range is formally in the IRBM class, although some sources call it an ICBM.
Its 5,000 km range is formally above the 5,500 km ICBM threshold.
accepted.x: The stated range of Agni-V is 5,000 km or more, while the formal ICBM threshold cited is 5,500 km. Therefore it is formally in the IRBM class in that classification, although some sources call it an ICBM.
accepted.tq: Separate informal descriptions from the stated technical threshold.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Agni-VI, in the context of India’s missile programme, is described as a:
accepted.x: Agni-VI is described as a proposed longer-range intercontinental ballistic missile.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a proposed future system from operational Agni variants.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Agni-Prime is correctly associated with which one of the following?
o: 5,000+ km range and three-stage solid propulsion
1,000–2,000 km range and canisterised new-generation design
9 km range and thrust vector control
accepted.x: Agni-Prime has a range of 1,000–2,000 km and is a new-generation canisterised missile.
accepted.tq: Match the variant with its distinctive range and design generation.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The launch associated with Agni-Prime on 24 September 2025 involved a:
accepted.x: Agni-Prime was fired from a rail-based mobile launcher on 24 September 2025.
accepted.tq: Link the date to the specific launch platform.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Agni missile programme is correct?
o: Agni is built by DRDO, is fully indigenous and is operated by the Strategic Forces Command.
Agni is built by ISRO and operated by the Air Force alone.
Agni is built by the Army and operated by the Navy.
Agni is jointly built by UNEP and DRDO for civilian satellite launch.
accepted.x: Agni is developed by DRDO, is fully indigenous and is operated by the Strategic Forces Command. It uses specialised navigation for accuracy.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who developed it and who operates it’ test.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mission Divyastra is associated with which one of the following developments?
o: Testing of MIRV capability on Agni-V in 2024
Development of the Akash missile’s liquid-fuel engine
accepted.x: Mission Divyastra, conducted in 2024, involved Agni-V with Multiple Independently targetable Re-entry Vehicles (MIRVs).
accepted.tq: Associate the named mission with its specific missile technology.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Agni-related events in chronological order:
A. Mission Divyastra involving Agni-V MIRV capability
B. Agni-Prime rail-based mobile-launcher firing
C. Advanced Agni test with MIRV under Strategic Forces Command
D. Agni-1 test from ITR Balasore
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The sequence is Mission Divyastra in 2024, Agni-Prime firing on 24 September 2025, Agni-1 test on 22 May 2026, and the advanced Agni MIRV test on 8 May 2026. Since 8 May precedes 22 May, the correct sequence is A, B, C, D.
accepted.tq: First identify the years, then resolve the 2026 events by exact dates.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Agni tests reported in 2026 were conducted under the authority of the:
accepted.x: The advanced Agni MIRV test, Agni-1 test and Agni-4 user trial reported in 2026 were conducted under the Strategic Forces Command.
accepted.tq: Identify the operational authority instead of the missile developer.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following correctly matches the 2026 Agni tests with their dates and locations?
1. Agni-1 — ITR Balasore — 22 May 2026
2. Agni-4 — ITR Chandipur — 6 August 2026
3. Advanced Agni with MIRV — 8 May 2026
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three matches are correct: the advanced Agni MIRV test occurred on 8 May 2026, Agni-1 was tested from ITR Balasore on 22 May 2026, and Agni-4 from ITR Chandipur on 6 August 2026.
accepted.tq: Match each test with both its date and test location.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Agni missiles are operated by the Strategic Forces Command.
Reason (R): Agni is a strategic ballistic-missile family developed by DRDO for indigenous long-range defence capability.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both the assertion and reason are true. However, the fact that DRDO developed Agni for indigenous strategic capability does not by itself explain the organisational assignment of its operation to the Strategic Forces Command.
accepted.tq: Check separately whether the reason explains the administrative relationship.
accepted.sec: Agni series - range, propellant, tests, ICBM status  [APPSC]
